.KEY MESSAGES...
Updated at 528 AM CDT Mon Sep 28 2026

- Widespread beneficial and potentially flooding rainfall 
  expected beginning late Tuesday through the end of the week. 

- Chance of severe storms Wednesday afternoon and Wednesday night.

- Temperatures will remain above normal through mid-week, before
  cooling Thursday into the weekend. 

&&

.NEAR TERM...
(Through Monday)
Issued at 129 AM CDT Mon Sep 28 2026

There will continue to be some isolated to widely scattered 
showers/storms across portions of central into south central and 
southeast Oklahoma early this morning. This may linger into this 
afternoon across far southeast Oklahoma, closer to weak upper 
forcing from departing shortwave trough. Otherwise, shortwave 
ridging aloft will be centered from southwest Texas through Oklahoma 
and northeast into the Upper Midwest. This is expected to keep 
much of the area dry through the day today. 

This upper shortwave ridge will also keep daytime temperatures well 
above normal for late September. Highs will range from the low/mid 
80s in the north to middle 90s in western north Texas. 

&&

.SHORT TERM...
(Monday night through Wednesday night)
Issued at 129 AM CDT Mon Sep 28 2026

By Tuesday, an upper trough will dig south across California and 
then close off and slow down as it turns east into the desert 
southwest. In advance of this trough southwest flow will pull 
increasing amounts of Pacific moisture northward, including the 
remnants of Hurricane Polo.

Although the main forcing from the upper low will be well west of 
the area during the day Tuesday. A lead wave will move northeast 
through west Texas and western Oklahoma producing showers and 
thunderstorms across western into northern Oklahoma. However, by 
Tuesday night and through the day Wednesday rain/storm chances 
increase, initially across the west, then expand eastward as the 
upper low approaches the Southern Plains.

Models are still suggesting a fairly well-defined dry slot 
developing during the day Wednesday from southwest Texas into 
western Oklahoma. In addition a dryline looks to set up, but the 
question is just where will this occur. Quite a range with this 
evenings models. The NAM would suggest the eastern Texas panhandle, 
the 12Z Euro is similar, but the 00Z GFS comes in much farther east 
as an elongated surface low runs from north-central Kansas into 
southwest Oklahoma with the dryline running closer to the I_44 
corridor. 

With either of these solutions, but especially with the further west 
scenario, there appears to be a window of opportunity for severe 
storms. Rather strong deep-layer shear and modest MUCAPE along with 
soundings showing a rather deeply saturated profile would suggest a 
chance for a tornado or two. If storms could entrain some dry air 
associated with the dry slot, large hail may be a concern as well. 
Still quite a bit of uncertainty with regards to severe potential 
however.

Otherwise, widespread appreciable and possibly flooding rainfall is 
expected from late Tuesday night through Wednesday night as the 
closed low progresses very slowly eastward through the area. 

&&

.LONG TERM...
(Thursday through Sunday)
Issued at 129 AM CDT Mon Sep 28 2026

As we go into the latter part of the week into the weekend, models 
differ on how they handle the upper low, but either solution(GFS or 
Euro) would keep precip chances in the forecast through the end of 
the week and through the upcoming weekend. Still heavy rainfall 
potential continues Thursday into Friday across south central and 
southeast parts of the state.

With this continuation of rain, associated cloud cover and frontal 
passage that will occur late in the week, temperatures will finally 
begin to feel more like fall instead of summer. Most areas from 
Thursday into at least Saturday will in the 70s and lower 80s. There 
is a chance for a few locations, especially Friday as cooler surface 
high pokes south into the area, to see highs only in the 60s. 

&&

.AVIATION...
(12Z TAFS)
Issued at 528 AM CDT Mon Sep 28 2026

Observations show an expansive area of fog and low ceilings in
southwest KS this morning. Given the amount of rain far northwest
OK has seen in the last 4-5 days, seems reasonable to assume areas
of (non-dense, in all likelihood) fog will impact the area 
between 12 and 16 UTC. After that, the general rule at terminals 
will be southeast winds and VFR skies through tomorrow morning.

Meister
